summary: Placeholder launch post saying the 2025 website was still under construction and linking last year's site.

Four weeks before departure, the team test-ran two learning festival workshops (Bottle Rocket and Phases of Matter) for students at Carbone Hall in Framingham, MA. The rocket did not lift off, and the food dye was too strong.
learning_festival: Test run at Carbone Hall, Framingham MA (juvenile detention facility and high school). Bottle Rocket (Charles, Joseph) and Phases of Matter (Greta, Ishaq: ice cube melting race, marshmallow molecules, oobleck).
contacts: Thomas Guarente, principal, Carbone Hall (Framingham, MA), made the learning festival possible
Ms. Gabbie and Paul, Carbone Hall staff, gave feedback on the first workshop iteration
planning_notes: Do a full dry run of each workshop the night before. The team's Phases of Matter food dye ratios were too strong and left blue hands.
Bottle rocket launch from baking soda and vinegar failed in the test run. Test the launch setup before the event.

summary: Charles and Ruth picked up the team's 2024 Chrysler Pacifica (named Amy), loaded roof and bike racks, and drove from Boston toward DC, lunching with Spokes 2017 alum Caity in Philly. The rest of the team gathered in DC for a kickoff dinner.
slept_at: Airbnb in DC
contacts: Caity, Spokes 2017 alum, Philadelphia (lunch, advice)
The Lawlers, kickoff team dinner in DC
planning_notes: Roof storage and bike rack assembly on the minivan went smoothly once the parts were staged. Boston to DC was a long, sleep-deprived drive with the loaded car.

summary: Team ran learning festivals at a DC Department of Corrections facility and at the Youth Services Center, then did errands in the city. Night was spent packing and setting up bikes.
slept_at: Airbnb in DC
learning_festival: DC Department of Corrections Correctional Treatment Facility (DOC) and Youth Services Center (YSC). Greta taught phases of matter, Ramona taught Caesar cipher cryptography, and the team ran five activities on rotation at YSC. Team also visited the YME unit at DOC.
contacts: Judge Faruqui, DOC (DC)
Ms. Reason, DOC (DC), let the team into the facility
Fiona and Brie, DOC (DC)
planning_notes: Corrections facilities use airport-style screening with no electronics allowed and several metal doors. Plan supply check-in ahead of time.
DC traffic is heavy and parking is expensive. The team used a car rental office visit and an alley drop-off to avoid parking costs.
Driving a loaded minivan with a bike rack through tight DC alleys is hard for a driver new to automatics.

summary: First riding day: DC area to Linden, VA (82 miles, 5,361 ft) over gravel roads, flats, and steep hills. A thunderstorm hit near the host, and the van had to shuttle stranded riders in.
slept_at: MIT alum Jen and Tim's home, Linden, VA (hosts)
contacts: Jen and Tim, MIT alum hosts, Linden, VA
Sarah's second cousin Claire and her husband Miles, rest stop near the route in VA (family provided bagels, fruit, and water refills)
planning_notes: Flats were frequent on the first 30 miles. Carry tubes and tools.
A severe storm hit at the Linden host. Keep the van's back seats clear so it can pick up riders caught in weather.
Several riders learned late that their bike had two sets of gears and rode the hardest setting all day. Teach gear use before day 1.
Steep climbs were hard for riders with health conditions. The van is a useful backup for a rider who needs to stop climbing.

summary: Linden, VA to Big Meadows Campground (55.75 miles, 6,555 ft). Riders climbed about 10 miles and 3,000 ft into Shenandoah National Park in heat, and the group reached the campground at sunset.
slept_at: Big Meadows Campground (Shenandoah National Park)
contacts: Jen, Tim, and baby Wayne, Linden, VA (hosts, pre-ride breakfast)
planning_notes: The Skyline climb into Shenandoah is about 10 miles and 3,000 ft at grade 5. Some riders needed the van for part of it.
Water ran out before the first rest stop in heat. Buy water at the cafe or gas stop before the climb.
Big Meadows general store closes around sunset. Buy food and supplies before you arrive.
Riders got separated at camp after dark. Agree on a regroup point and a plan for a late arrival.

summary: Big Meadows to Afton, VA (42.74 miles, 3,045 ft). Fog, blind curves, and heavy rain made the Skyline Drive descent unsafe, so riders and bikes were shuttled down by car, and the team reached the host by about 5 pm.
slept_at: Pam Mendosa's home, Shannon Farm intentional community, Afton, VA (2 nights)
contacts: Pam Mendosa, Shannon Farm, Afton, VA (hosted two nights)
Greg, and Captain Lawler (Greta's dad), who shuttled riders and bikes down from Big Meadows in two cars
planning_notes: Skyline Drive descent in fog, rain, and blind curves was unsafe for riders. Plan a rain-day bailout and a car shuttle for bikes.
Two cars with two bike racks still did not fit all bikes in one trip. Count rack capacity before the shuttle.
Pam Mendosa (Shannon Farm, Afton VA) is an excellent host. Her property is off-grid, and there is no wifi or cell service there.

summary: Rest day at Pam's property in Afton, VA. The team dried soaked camping gear and cleaned bikes, then went to Charlottesville for laundry, a bike shop repair of broken spokes, and a coffee-shop work session. They also spent hours arguing over the next day's route.
slept_at: Pam Mendosa's home, Afton, VA
contacts: Blue Wheel Bicycles, Charlottesville, VA (repaired broken spokes)
Shenandoah Joe Coffee Roasters, Charlottesville, VA (work spot with wifi)
planning_notes: Pam's house has no dryer, no wifi, and no cell service. Do laundry and laptop work in Charlottesville.
Route planning took hours. The next day's route was changed to a shorter but steeper climb of over 3,000 ft.

summary: Afton to Lexington, VA (47 miles, 4,354 ft). The route included the steepest climb of the trip, averaging 10% with a maximum of 17%. The team reached a Warmshowers host by 3:30 pm.
slept_at: Dirk and Chrissy's home, Lexington, VA (Warmshowers host)
contacts: Dirk and Chrissy, Warmshowers hosts, Lexington, VA
planning_notes: Climb out of Afton: average 10% grade, max 17%. It is steeper than an ADA wheelchair ramp limit, so expect walking.

The team shares one bike computer and rotates it among drivers. When one driver's computer failed to load the route, the rider had to follow another rider. Keep a backup route on paper or a second device.
Warmshowers host had a dog and a foot massager, and the team was able to shower and cook early. Arriving early at hosts gives time for group activities.

summary: Lexington to Roanoke, VA (59.6 miles, 4,160 ft). Riders split up and rode at their own pace, and one rider missed the first rest stop. The hosts took the team sightseeing to Roanoke's large star after arrival.
slept_at: Lisa and Rob's home, Roanoke, VA
contacts: Lisa and Rob, Roanoke, VA (hosts; Rob created the Virginia Rockstar route)
Carol, Rob's mother, Roanoke, VA (fan of Spokes)
planning_notes: Leaving Lexington, a grassy and gravel path crosses a creaky bridge. Some riders felt unsafe on it.
Open-ear headphones (a tip from a former Spokes rider, Duha) helped one rider keep pedaling on a long day.
Roanoke's large star is a good afternoon sightseeing stop for the team when arriving early.

summary: Roanoke to Radford, VA (52.4 miles, 4,265 ft), written by the driver. It covers the daily driver role, a failed scratch-off stop, a cooler with unloaded cans, a tuna can with no opener, and dinner and s'mores with the host in Radford.
slept_at: Sharon and Keith's home, Radford, VA
contacts: Sharon and Keith, Radford, VA (hosts; fried spaghetti dinner, greenhouse tour)
planning_notes: Driver duties: unload the cooler the night before, pack the car, refill water jugs, flag riders down at rest stops, contact hosts, check rider locations on Life360, and handle shopping and gas.
Keep at most one bag on top of the cooler so lunches are easy to reach.
Check that every drink is in the cooler. Unloaded cans burst in the heat.
Keep the can opener in an easy-to-reach box, not under others in the trunk.

summary: Radford to Tazewell, VA (68.2 miles, 4,380 ft). The day felt long and hot, and a podcast got one rider through the slow middle miles. The team stopped for ice cream and reached the church host in Tazewell.
slept_at: Main Street United Methodist Church, Tazewell, VA (church host)
contacts: Theresa, Main Street United Methodist Church, Tazewell, VA (host)
planning_notes: Navigation devices read about 6,000 ft of climbing for this route, while RideWithGPS showed about 4,300 ft. Expect the higher number.
A reported hornet's nest was near a rest stop. Check rest stops for wildlife (unconfirmed).
Tazewell's ice cream shop sells floats, and an Italian restaurant shares the same building. Good stop for a team meal.

summary: Learning festival day at Main Street United Methodist Church in Tazewell, VA, with four age groups from kindergarten through high school. Sarah and Joseph were floaters and ran the bottle rocket demo for church members and kids at lunch. Laundry and an ice cream treat followed.
slept_at: Main Street United Methodist Church, Tazewell, VA
learning_festival: Main Street UMC, Tazewell, VA, with four age groups (kindergarten through high school). Greta: states of matter with melting ice and oobleck. Ruth and Charles: 3D printing and pens. Ramona: Caesar cipher cryptography. Tian and Ishaq: machine learning and AI. Sarah and Joseph: bottle rockets (floaters, demo at lunch).
contacts: Theresa, Main Street UMC, Tazewell, VA (learning festival contact; treated the team to ice cream and bought new towels)
Church members (lunch and breakfast, vinegar donated)
planning_notes: Mixed-age groups are hard. The team adjusted each lesson for its age group, and high schoolers needed a different version than kindergarteners.
Church members assumed the bottle rocket was firecracker-powered. Explain the baking soda and vinegar mechanism to hosts before the event.
Bring extra quarters. Three laundry loads took about 68 quarters at the laundromat.

summary: Tazewell, VA toward Breaks Interstate Park. A rain storm hit at the Honaker Community Center, and the team split on whether to stay there. Ishaq's front derailleur broke, and he finished on a bike with only the big ring. The campsite was the wrong one, and a ranger said it was fine.
slept_at: Breaks Interstate Park campground (team was on the wrong site; a ranger said it was fine since no one had booked it)
contacts: Honaker Community Center staff (would not allow riders to stay the night indoors)
planning_notes: Honaker Community Center does not allow overnight stays inside. Ask before planning a stop there.
A misaligned front derailleur left a rider stuck in the big ring for the last 30 miles. Bring tools and know how to adjust a derailleur.
Cell service dropped on the final climbs toward Breaks Interstate Park. Download the route offline and agree on regroup points.
Descents at 30 mph in heavy rain are dangerous. Stop and wait out storms at the base of a climb.

summary: Riders crossed from Virginia into eastern Kentucky on a rainy, rural day. The team went around for rose, thorn, and bud reflections. Saddle sores and unleashed dogs came up often.
planning_notes: Rural eastern Kentucky is sparse on services. Plan food and water between stops; there was a Dairy Queen stop.
Saddle sores were the most common difficulty by day 12. Get a saddle and shorts fit checked before the trip.
Unleashed dogs were a recurring fear for riders in Kentucky.

summary: Learning festival day at the Challenger Learning Center in Hazard, KY. Sarah had an allergy scare and took Benadryl, so Joseph ran bottle rockets alone. Ishaq drove two hours to fix his bike, and Tian ran machine learning alone.
slept_at: Harmony House B&B, Hazard, KY
learning_festival: Challenger Learning Center, Hazard, KY. Kids from kindergarten through 9th grade in separate groups. Bottle rockets (Joseph, solo), machine learning (Tian), 3D printing (Charles and Ruth). Afterward, the team toured the center's Mission Mars simulation and exhibit space.
contacts: Sherry, Harmony House B&B, Hazard, KY (breakfast casserole)
Challenger Learning Center staff, Hazard, KY (tour, catered Italian dinner)
planning_notes: Bottle rocket lessons that work for young kids bored older kids (grades 6 to 9). Group students by age and prepare an advanced version.
3D printing for 40+ kids is the hardest workshop to run. Plan time for printing and handing out prints, since some kids did not get theirs.
Bike shop repairs can mean a two-hour drive each way from Hazard, KY (Lexington). Carry spare parts and tools.
The Challenger Learning Center has simulated space missions and an exhibit space. Good stop for kids and the team.

summary: Hazard, KY to London, KY (70.7 miles, 5,293 ft) on single-lane backroads through a humid forest. A flooded road forced a reroute onto Hell for Certain Rd (Sizerock), and riders arrived in a thunderstorm at golden hour.
contacts: Locals at a Spring Rd crossing near Sizerock, KY (warned about flooding and gave the reroute)
planning_notes: Backroads out of Hazard are a single lane, with gravel, steep ascents, and streams. Some roads flood after rain.
Ask locals before committing to a road at a junction. Locals at Spring Rd knew a flooded road and a dead end, and they gave a safe alternative.
Hell for Certain Rd (Sizerock) is steep and rough gravel. The van struggled, and riders were shuttled in some sections.
Local homes keep territorial dogs and kids on quadricycles. Dogs often chase bikes here.

summary: Tian had a rough day in heat with dizziness and could not finish the route, so she rode in the van for the last 30 miles. There was a near-miss at a stop sign with a car. The team ate a group dinner at Liberty Assembly of God Church.
slept_at: Liberty Assembly of God Church, Liberty, KY
contacts: Liberty Assembly of God Church, Liberty, KY (overnight host)
planning_notes: Rural Kentucky stretches can go a long time without a restroom. Carry toilet paper, and ask nearby homes early (many have barking dogs).
Chewable electrolytes and energy gel helped a rider with dizziness. Drivers should check on riders in heat and offer a ride early.
Stop signs on hills are dangerous when riders are tired. Stop fully and check for traffic.
The team set a 9 am departure at the group meeting to start earlier in the heat.

summary: Liberty, KY to Mammoth Cave National Park (88.6 miles, 5,465 ft), the longest ride so far. Ruth was sick and rode in the van. Riders bought a bucket of Lee's Famous Chicken at a rest stop, a bike shop traded a pump for free, and the team had a campfire dinner at the Mammoth Cave campground.
slept_at: Mammoth Cave National Park campground
contacts: Bike shop owner in Kentucky (traded a used pump for free)
planning_notes: A rural stream crossing on this route is not rideable. Dismount and walk your bike across.
Greta took a wrong turn and added 4 miles. Confirm turns when riders split up.
Save A Lot did not have marshmallows, foil, or firewood. Buy them in a bigger store.
Firewood was available at the Mammoth Cave campground.
Lee's Famous Chicken bucket at a Campbellsville rest stop was the team's favorite rest stop. Plan a food stop there.

summary: Short day from Mammoth Cave to Bowling Green (32.7 miles, 1,342 ft). The team took a self-guided Mammoth Cave tour, rode to the Buc-ee's rest stop in Smith's Grove, KY, then rode the last 17 miles into Bowling Green in rain.
slept_at: Airbnb in Bowling Green, KY (provided by learning festival partners)
planning_notes: Book a guided Mammoth Cave tour ahead. The self-guided line wasted time.
Buc-ee's in Smith's Grove, KY is a full-service rest stop with clean restrooms, food, and a big bike rack area. The team loved it.
Flash rain hit about 3 miles before Bowling Green. Carry rain gear on afternoon rides.

summary: Rest day in Bowling Green, KY. The team had breakfast at the Airbnb, Sarah worked from Spencer's Coffee, and everyone cooked burrito night at the house. Sarah reflected on the first 20 days.
slept_at: Airbnb in Bowling Green, KY (provided by learning festival partners)
contacts: Learning festival partners in Bowling Green, KY (provided the Airbnb and recommended Spencer's Coffee)
planning_notes: Spencer's Coffee in Bowling Green is a good laptop work spot. It closes at 6 pm.
Insomnia Cookies is a short walk from the Bowling Green Airbnb.
Bowling Green's heat was 85 to 90 degrees Fahrenheit and humid on a rest day.

summary: Bowling Green learning festival day. The machine learning lesson went well: kids built data sets to train a 'happiness detector', and the team tested new extensions to the lesson.
learning_festival: Bowling Green, KY. Machine learning lesson taught by Tian and Ishaq. Kids built data to train a 'happiness detector', and the team tested new extensions covering other types of machine learning problems.
planning_notes: The 'happiness detector' data-collection activity worked well with kids. The first class got the first activity right on the first try.
Plan extensions for fast finishers in the ML lesson.

summary: Bowling Green, KY to Madisonville, KY (84.8 miles, 4,439 ft) in a heat wave with temperatures in the high 90s before noon. The team hosted two WKU students they met at the Bowling Green learning festival for dinner, and stayed at Life Christian Center.
slept_at: Life Christian Center, Madisonville, KY (church gymnasium)
learning_festival: Bowling Green, KY (the day before). Bottle rocket workshop. Khalil, from the WKU Small Business Accelerator, helped run the festival. Libby, a WKU Herald summer intern, covered the event.
contacts: Khalil, WKU Small Business Accelerator, Bowling Green, KY (education startup; helped run the festival)
Libby, WKU Herald summer intern, Bowling Green, KY (covered the festival)
Pastor Jon, Isaac, and Steve, Life Christian Center, Madisonville, KY (hosts; home-cooked dinner)
planning_notes: The heat wave started with highs in the high 90s before noon. Leave by about 8 am and carry extra electrolytes.
Church gymnasiums work as overnight stops. Bring a sleeping pad and expect a hard floor.
Pack leftovers for lunch. Tian's leftover-first approach worked well on hot days.

summary: Madisonville, KY to Harrisburg, IL (90.3 miles, 2,533 ft). Joseph had heat exhaustion and back pain and got in the van at a rest stop, then rode the last segment with Tian. The route crossed the Ohio River on the Shawneetown Bridge into Illinois, and the team was hosted by Sherry in Harrisburg.
slept_at: Sherry's home, Harrisburg, IL
contacts: Sherry, Harrisburg, IL (host; watermelon and dinner)
4 S Dairy Barn, Illinois (ice cream rest stop; posted the team on Facebook)
planning_notes: Heat exhaustion hit riders in late June. Riders who had spent rest days indoors in air conditioning had less heat acclimation. Build heat exposure into training or early days.
Back pain from a bike fit problem was fixed later. Get a bike fit check before the trip.
The Shawneetown Bridge crosses the Ohio River into Illinois.

summary: Harrisburg, IL to Murphysboro, IL (51.6 miles, 1,314 ft), driven by Ruth. Tian crashed on a gravel turn, and Sarah cleaned her wounds with the first-aid kit. Ruth drove an hour back to Harrisburg for a forgotten bike bib, which was picked up at a Walmart Supercenter.
slept_at: Jessica's home, Murphysboro, IL (host)
contacts: Jessica, Murphysboro, IL (host)
Sherie, Harrisburg, IL (host; arranged the bib pickup at a Walmart Supercenter)
planning_notes: A gravel turn about 2 miles before Crown Brew Coffee Co. caused a crash. Slow down on gravel corners.
Before leaving a host, check that all laundry (including bibs drying in the bathroom) is packed.
Big grocery runs overfill the cooler. Plan for what fits.
The next day's route was over 100 miles, leaving at 7 am.
